Two war poems, a century apart. How do you compare, not list?
Why squeeze a love story into exactly fourteen lines?

component-2-post-1914-prose-drama-19th-c: One printed scene, a question on the whole play. Where do you start?
Dickens attacked workhouses. When does knowing that earn marks?
A poem you've never seen, twenty minutes. What do you look for first?
Two war poems, a century apart. How do you compare, not list?
Two essays, same quotations; one scores double. What's different?
poetry-anthology: He loves to learn. So what is Blake's schoolboy protesting about?
Why does a poem about daffodils end on a couch?
It opens 'I think of thee!' and ends 'I do not'. Why?
Cast off for her cousin, she ends with a 'gift'. Who has won?
Buried far from home under strange stars. Does Hodge belong now?
A sonnet full of happy memories. Why does the last word say 'pain'?
Why does "Disabled" keep jumping between then and now?
macbeth: A brave hero in Act 1, a 'dead butcher' by Act 5. What went wrong?
Macbeth argues himself out of murder. Why does he do it anyway?
She begs spirits to 'unsex me here'. So why does she crack first?
The witches never tell Macbeth to kill. So are they to blame?
Macbeth sees a dagger, then a ghost. Are they real?
Why does killing a king make horses eat each other?
Verse, prose, rhyme: why does Shakespeare change how people speak?
romeo-and-juliet: The Prologue gives away the ending. Why would Shakespeare do that?
Romeo loves Rosaline, then Juliet, in one night. Fickle or changed?
Juliet obeys her parents in Act 1. By Act 3 she defies them. Why?
The greatest love story ever, or a warning about rushing in?
No one says why the feud began. So why does everyone keep fighting?
Meet on Sunday, wed on Monday, dead within the week. Why the rush?
The lovers only meet in the dark. Why is their love always light?
othello: Blissful in Act 2, a murderer by Act 5. How did it happen so fast?
Noble general or jealous killer: which is the real Othello?
Iago tells us why he hates Othello. Should we believe him?
Desdemona defies her father, then won't defy her husband. Why?
There is no affair. So where does Othello's jealousy come from?
Venice needs Othello to fight. Does it ever accept him?
By Act 4 Othello talks like Iago. How did Iago get into his words?
much-ado-about-nothing: Two love stories, one play. Why does Shakespeare need both?
They trade insults at every meeting. Why do they end up married?
Claudio shames Hero at the altar. Does he deserve her at the end?
Two tricks by overhearing: one makes love, one nearly kills. Why?
One rumour, and Hero's own father wishes her dead. Why?
The play opens as soldiers come home. Why start a comedy with a war?
Most of the play is prose. So why does Beatrice switch to rhyme?
twelfth-night: A love story and a prank on a steward. Why put both in one play?
Viola could just tell Orsino the truth. Why stay in disguise?
Malvolio is tricked, mocked and locked in the dark. Funny or cruel?
Orsino says he's sick with love. Does he love Olivia, or love itself?
A boy plays a girl playing a boy. What does Shakespeare do with that?
The play is named for a party night. Who rules once the party starts?
The fool may be the wisest person in the play. How can that be?
the-merchant-of-venice: Three weddings and a happy ending. So why do many audiences not laugh?
He demands a pound of flesh. Villain, victim, or both?
Gold, silver or lead: why does the dullest casket hold the prize?
Is the play antisemitic, or is it about antisemitism?
Shylock wins in law, then loses everything. Is that justice or mercy?
In this play, is a bond about money or about love?
Every big speech in this play tries to persuade. Which ones work?
a-christmas-carol: Why does Scrooge's whole life change in a single night?
Does Scrooge change overnight, or was the change already in him?
Tiny Tim barely speaks. Why does the book end on his words?
Why does the last ghost never say a single word?
Who should help the poor: the law, charity or Scrooge himself?
Scrooge pays his taxes. Why isn't that enough for Dickens?
Fog, frost, fire: why does the weather change as Scrooge does?
silas-marner: Why does the novel jump sixteen years in the middle?
What turns a man who loved gold into a man who loves people?
Godfrey is Eppie's real father. Why does she turn him down?
Silas loses his faith in a chapel. Where does he find it again?
Silas mistakes a child's curls for gold. Why make them alike?
Godfrey keeps his secret and his status. Does he get away with it?
Why does Eliot replace Silas's old chapel with a factory?
the-war-of-the-worlds: One man tells the story. How does he describe scenes he never saw?
Hero or coward: what kind of man is telling this story?
The Martians are monsters. So why do they look like our future?
Earth's mightiest invaders are killed by germs. Is that a cheat?
Why would a British novel make Britain the conquered country?
When the Martians come, what breaks first: buildings or people?
What did a reader in 1897 see in this story that we miss?
pride-and-prejudice: The novel's first line states a 'truth'. Should you believe it?
Elizabeth trusts her judgement of people. Should we trust it too?
Darcy insults Elizabeth at their first ball. Who changes?
Charlotte marries a man she can't respect. Foolish or wise?
Lady Catherine says Elizabeth isn't good enough. Does the novel agree?
Lydia runs off with Wickham. Who is to blame?
Austen rarely writes 'she thought'. So whose voice are you reading?
jane-eyre: Five homes, one girl. Why does Jane's story keep moving her on?
Poor, plain, little: why is Jane Eyre so hard to silence?
Rochester deceives Jane. Why does the novel reunite them?
A girl locked in the red-room, a wife locked upstairs. Why both?
Does Jane end the novel free, or just married?
Brocklehurst, Helen, St John: whose faith does Jane choose?
"Reader, I married him." Why does Jane keep talking to you?
the-strange-case-of-dr-jekyll-and-mr-hyd: Why does the novel hide its biggest secret until the last chapter?
Is Hyde a monster the potion made, or Jekyll all along?
Utterson is a lawyer. Why can't he solve the case?
A man is murdered. Why do his friends worry about a good name?
Is Jekyll's potion science, sin or magic?
Why do so many characters describe Hyde like an animal?
Why does the fog never seem to lift on this London?
